speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. To begin our evaluation of your acute diarrhea, how long have you been experiencing these symptoms and what is their frequency?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old female. The patient has been treated for community-acquired pneumonia with levofloxacin on the medical floor. She reports developing watery diarrhea with at least 9 episodes within the last two days, accompanied by lower abdominal discomfort and cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Clostridioides difficile infection (C. diff). The patient's history of recent levofloxacin use for pneumonia, combined with acute watery diarrhea and abdominal cramping, is highly suggestive of antibiotic-associated colitis. I will proceed with testing to confirm the diagnosis.
